newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end higher on late buying surge.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end higher on late buying surge.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher with July bounding sharply higher late amid a surge of commission house buying, traders said.
A broker who takes telephone orders, said cash lumber trading increased Friday when cash spruce prices slipped to the mid-$350 per thousand board foot area, well under the latest official cash quote.
Random Lengths early Friday reported cash spruce prices dropped to $364 per tbf from $377 a week ago.
The buying in futures caught some traders by surprise, prompting them to cancel sell orders that had been positioned in the market.
A cash-connected trader said a fair amount of cash lumber traded at lower prices, but he doubted the demand would continue next week.
"There is still plenty of product around. I don't think this cash business is sustainable," he said.
CME lumber futures closed up $6.30 to down $0.10 with July up the most at $380.50 per tbf.
